prompt:
Rewrite snippets/bundle-eligibility-notice.liquid. It shows whether a cart qualifies for a product bundle. Every piece of user text must be HTML-escaped exactly once, both in element text and in attribute values. Inputs (all top-level variables, there is no section object): - `bundle`: object or null. When it is an object it always has both keys: - `bundle.title`: string or null. It may contain surrounding whitespace and the characters < > & " '. - `bundle.min_items`: integer >= 1, never null. - `cart_items`: array, always present, possibly empty. Each element always has both keys: - `title`: string, never null. It may contain < > & " '. - `eligible`: boolean or null. Only `true` counts as eligible; false and null do not. Rules: 1. If `bundle` is null, output nothing (empty string). 2. Display title T: take `bundle.title`, strip leading and trailing whitespace. If the result is empty (or the title is null), use `Bundle`. Then HTML-escape it with the core `escape` filter. Use the same escaped T in all three places below. 3. N = the number of eligible items in `cart_items`. 4. Output, with no whitespace or newlines between or inside tags: `

T

MESSAGE

LIST
` 5. MESSAGE: when N >= min_items it is `Bundle unlocked!`. Otherwise let R = min_items - N. The message is `Add R more eligible item to unlock T.` when R is 1, and `Add R more eligible items to unlock T.` for any other R. 6. LIST: when N is 0, output nothing. Otherwise output `
    ` followed by one `
  • I
    • ` per eligible item, in input order, then `
`. I is the item title HTML-escaped (not stripped). Ineligible items are never listed. Example: title `Mix & Match ` becomes `Mix & Match <Deluxe>`. A double quote becomes `"` and an apostrophe becomes `'`. Output only the specified elements/attributes; escape dynamic text and attributes. Inter-element whitespace, comments and quote style may vary; leaf text is exact. Change only snippets/bundle-eligibility-notice.liquid. Do not suppress checks or hardcode case values. All input keys are present.
